newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korean captain arrested in Japan drug case.
newsitem.headline: North Korean captain arrested in Japan drug case.

text.p: Police in southern Japan arrested the captain of a North Korea freighter which was seized with a large cache of illegal drugs this month, a police spokesman said.

The 50-year-old captain, whose nationality was North Korean but whose name was not disclosed, was the third figure arrested on suspicion of smuggling stimulants in cargo labelled as honey on the North Korean-registered freighter Ji Song-2.

Two Koreans from an Osaka-based trading firm were arrested last week for suspected involvement in smuggling 70 kg (154 lb) of amphetamines, with a street value estimated at 11.9 billion yen ($95 million).

The drugs were found when the 1,499-tonne North Korean freighter, which left the North Korean port of Nanpo on April 5, was searched at the Japanese port of Hososhima on the Pacific coast of Kyushu island, police said.
Japanese analysts have said the drug smuggling could be a sign that North Korea, impoverished and facing near-famine conditions has turned to new means to raise cash from Japan.
Donations to Pyongyang by residents of Japan of North Korean descent, a legacy of Tokyo's 1910-45 colonisation of Korea, are a key source of hard currency for the isolated Stalinist government.
